```
bin/payout run 20261005                    # extract → build → ship

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# payout — merchant settlement files for card-acquiring partners.
#
#   payout run DATE                  extract → build → ship
#   payout manifest DATE             files handed to the transfer CLI that day
#   payout receipts PARTNER FROM TO  what the partner can download, per day
#   payout partners                  active partner codes
#
# DATE is YYYYMMDD. Configuration: conf/payout.conf (PAYOUT_* overrides).
set -u
export LC_ALL=C.UTF-8
PAYOUT_HOME=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
export PAYOUT_HOME
. "$PAYOUT_HOME/steps/_env.sh"

usage() { sed -n '3,9p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }

cmd_run() {
  local date=$1 step rc
  for step in "$PAYOUT_HOME"/steps/[0-9][0-9]-*.sh; do
    bash "$step" "$date"
    rc=$?
    if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
      warn "step $(basename "$step") failed (exit $rc)"
      return "$rc"
    fi
  done
  log "run $date complete"
}

cmd_manifest() {
  local date=$1 p name ticket rows

# chunk.sh M-bM-^@M-^T splits a row file into parts of at most N rows.

# chunk_rows FILE MAX PREFIX M-bM-^@M-^T writes PREFIX.01, PREFIX.02, ... and prints the
# number of parts. An empty FILE still yields one (empty) part so the partner
# receives a file for every settlement day.
chunk_rows() {
  local file=$1 max=$2 prefix=$3 rows parts
  rows=$(wc -l < "$file" | tr -d ' ')
  if [ "$rows" -le "$max" ]; then
    cp -f "$file" "$prefix.01" || return 1
    printf '1'
    return 0
  fi
  split -l "$max" -d -a 2 --numeric-suffixes=1 "$file" "$prefix." || return 1
  parts=$(( (rows + max - 1) / max ))
  printf '%d' "$parts"
}
==== lib/csvfile.sh
# csvfile.sh M-bM-^@M-^T settlement file body (PAY-IF-03 rev.2).
#
#   H,<sender>,<partner>,<date>,<part>/<parts>
#   D,<txn>,<date>,<amount>,<fee>,<net>      one per transaction
#   T,<detail count>,<net total>
#
# Lines end in CRLF when LINE_END=crlf.

_eol() { [ "${LINE_END:-lf}" = crlf ] && printf '\r\n' || printf '\n'; }

# csv_render DATE PARTNER PART PARTS < rows(txn<TAB>amount<TAB>fee)
csv_render() {
  local date=$1 partner=$2 part=$3 parts=$4 txn amount fee net n=0 total=0
  printf 'H,%s,%s,%s,%d/%d' "$SENDER_ID" "$partner" "$date" "$part" "$parts"; _eol
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r txn amount fee; do
    [ -n "$txn" ] || continue
    net=$(money_net "$amount" "$fee")
    printf 'D,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s' "$txn" "$date" "$amount" "$fee" "$net"; _eol
    n=$((n + 1)); total=$((total + net))
  done
  printf 'T,%d,%d' "$n" "$total"; _eol
}
==== lib/naming.sh
# naming.sh M-bM-^@M-^T remote file names for settlement files.
#
#   HBP_SETTLE_<partner>_<YYYYMMDD>.csv          one file for the day
#   HBP_SETTLE_<partner>_<YYYYMMDD>_<n>.csv      day split into several parts

# settle_name PARTNER DATE PART PARTS
settle_name() {
  local partner=$1 date=$2 part=$3 parts=$4
  local base="${FILE_PREFIX}_${partner}_${date}"
  if [ "$parts" -gt 1 ]; then
    base="${base}_${part}"
  fi
  printf '%s.%s' "$base" "$FILE_EXT"
}

# xfer.sh M-bM-^@M-^T thin wrapper around the transfer vendor CLI.

_xferq() { "$XFERQ" "$@"; }

# xfer_send PARTNER FILE NAME M-bM-^@M-^T uploads FILE as NAME and prints the ticket.
# Transient spool errors are retried; a malformed answer counts as a failure.
xfer_send() {

# money.sh — integer KRW arithmetic and formatting.

# money_net AMOUNT FEE -> amount minus fee
money_net() { printf '%d' $(( 10#$1 - 10#$2 )); }

# money_fmt N -> "1,234,567"
money_fmt() {
  local n=$1 sign="" out=""
  case "$n" in -*) sign="-"; n=${n#-} ;; esac
  while [ ${#n} -gt 3 ]; do
    out=",${n: -3}$out"

# "20261005" -> "2026-10-05"
date_dash() { printf '%s-%s-%s' "${1:0:4}" "${1:4:2}" "${1:6:2}"; }

date_compact() { local d=${1//-/}; printf '%s' "$d"; }

# date_next YYYYMMDD -> the following calendar day
date_next() { date -u -d "$(date_dash "$1") +1 day" +%Y%m%d; }

# Partners settle seven days a week, so weekends are included.
date_range() {
  local d=$1 end=$2 guard=0
  while [ "$d" -le "$end" ]; do
    printf '%s\n' "$d"

    guard=$((guard + 1))
    [ "$guard" -le 400 ] || { warn "date range too long: $1..$2"; return 1; }
  done

# txns.sh — reads the acquiring extract (settle_date, partner, txn, amount, fee).

# txns_for DATE PARTNER — that partner's rows for DATE, ordered by txn id.
txns_for() {
  require_file "$TXN_FILE" "transaction extract"
  awk -F'\t' -v d="$1" -v p="$2" '
    /^#/ || NF < 5 { next }
    $1 == d && $2 == p { print $3 "\t" $4 "\t" $5 }
  ' "$TXN_FILE" | sort -t$'\t' -k1,1
}

# txns_count DATE PARTNER

# money.sh — integer KRW arithmetic and formatting.

# money_net AMOUNT FEE -> amount minus fee
money_net() { printf '%d' $(( 10#$1 - 10#$2 )); }

# money_fmt N -> "1,234,567"
money_fmt() {
  local n=$1 sign="" out=""
  case "$n" in -*) sign="-"; n=${n#-} ;; esac
  while [ ${#n} -gt 3 ]; do
    out=",${n: -3}$out"
    n=${n:0:${#n}-3}
  done
  printf '%s%s%s' "$sign" "$n" "$out"
}

# dates.sh — business date helpers (GNU date).

# "20261005" -> "2026-10-05"
date_dash() { printf '%s-%s-%s' "${1:0:4}" "${1:4:2}" "${1:6:2}"; }

# "2026-10-05" or "20261005" -> "20261005"
date_compact() { local d=${1//-/}; printf '%s' "$d"; }

# date_next YYYYMMDD -> the following calendar day
date_next() { date -u -d "$(date_dash "$1") +1 day" +%Y%m%d; }

# date_range FROM TO — every calendar day from FROM to TO inclusive.
# Partners settle seven days a week, so weekends are included.
date_range() {
  local d=$1 end=$2 guard=0
  while [ "$d" -le "$end" ]; do
    printf '%s\n' "$d"
    d=$(date_next "$d")
    guard=$((guard + 1))
    [ "$guard" -le 400 ] || { warn "date range too long: $1..$2"; return 1; }
  done
